summary: TICKET-006 authored migration 20260927120000_ticketing_issuance_slot_dedup.sql, which adds three columns to the active chain: tickets.issuance_slot (integer, nullable), ticket_analytics_events.dedupe_key (text, nullable), ticket_sales.issuance_alerted_at (timestamptz, nullable). lib/database.types.ts is not in the ticketing working set and is not owned by this lane, so it has not been regenerated. This adds to drift that already exists: the TICKET-005 wave-35 migration 20260926130000_ticketing_webhook_completion_marker.sql added ticket_stripe_webhook_events.completed_at and .attempts, which the committed types also do not carry. The ticketing code does not currently need the generated types to compile — the issuance, analytics and finalize clients are typed as `from: (table: string) => any` — so this is a contract-completeness item, not a build break. Regenerate once the migration is applied (see HF-TICKET-006-ISSUANCE-DEDUP-APPLY for the apply, which is release's).
completed: Recorded the exact three columns the migration adds, with types and nullability, so regeneration does not have to re-derive them from the SQL.

Confirmed no ticketing file depends on the generated Row types for these three columns, so the drift is additive and non-breaking: lib/ticketing/issuance.ts, lib/ticketing/analytics.ts and lib/ticketing/finalize.ts all write through an untyped PostgREST client interface.

Confirmed the pre-existing drift this extends: rg for completed_at/attempts in lib/database.types.ts finds no ticket_stripe_webhook_events entry, so check:database-types was already failing for the wave-35 migration before TICKET-006.
next_steps: After HF-TICKET-006-ISSUANCE-DEDUP-APPLY applies the migration to a target, run npm run generate:database-types with the same SUPABASE_TYPE_SOURCE used for the target and commit the regenerated lib/database.types.ts.
Include ticket_stripe_webhook_events.completed_at and .attempts in that regeneration, so the wave-35 completion marker and this task's three keys land in one regeneration rather than two.
Re-run npm run check:database-types against the same type source and confirm the drift is closed.
blockers: The migration is authored and never applied, so there is no schema to generate types from; regeneration must follow the apply.
The database lane reports supabase start cannot bring up postgres on this box (disk at 6.7 GiB free), so local generation is unavailable.
verification: PASS: npx tsc -p <scoped tsconfig over the ticketing lib and webhook route> — no type errors attributable to the three ungenerated columns.
NOT RUN: npm run generate:database-types and npm run check:database-types — both require a live type source, which is unavailable locally and belongs to this receiving lane.
completion_condition: Regenerate lib/database.types.ts from a target that has 20260927120000 applied, covering tickets.issuance_slot, ticket_analytics_events.dedupe_key, ticket_sales.issuance_alerted_at and the wave-35 ticket_stripe_webhook_events.completed_at/.attempts, and confirm npm run check:database-types is clean against that type source.
